design_rationale:
WORKLOG - installation_service_desk, task 1 (Pinegrove Dental Partners fleet deployment invoice)
Revision 3, written after the second source-layer policy-task audit
(env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/installation_service_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md, sections
revision_2). Every figure has been recomputed on the amended charter and the amended seed; superseded figures are
named where they changed. Task 1's three golds are unchanged at 1275.00 / 846.50 / 1145.00 across revisions 2 and
3: revision 3's charter changes on these policies are guards, wordings and one re-keyed ladder, none of which move
the world this task takes.

STEP 0. Draw, pasted verbatim from
.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/installation_service_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/installation_service_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/installation_service_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}
Task 1 is a chain of three problems, two of them prerequisites, six declared factors on each computation.

WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. A practice manager rings to settle one invoice this morning. Behind that errand sits
a real unwind: the rollout was carried out as plan work and written off to the ShieldCare plan, the plan refused
the claim, and the labour must come back to the practice — at the service's own rate rather than the rate the line
was wrongly booked at, over the hours of both plan-work attendances, each attendance carrying the minimum hours
because this service sends two people, with the diagnostic fee credited and the plan-covered write-off
deliberately not set against it. Only then can the contract relief be worked out, which needs the included-visit
pool, the attendances the rebill covers and three attendance charges; and only then is the settlement fixed.
Three numbers in order, each reading rows the previous write created.

SCOPE. Claimed here: service_ext_declined_claim_labour_rebill, service_ext_business_contract_relief,
service_ext_invoice_settlement_payment with bill_uncovered_device_labour_51108cc0,
credit_contract_relief_ce7af535 and settle_deployment_invoice_642fded5. Task 0's three policies and three tools
are untouched, it reads the Circle membership across where this task reads the ShieldCare plan, and its deepest
problem is a fee where this one is chargeable labour.

POLICIES CLAIMED, THEIR LINEAGE AND EVERY DECLARED OVERRIDE. The revision-2 sweep went clause by clause through
the base policies these subjects touch and added one declaration and kept one:
- service_ext_declined_claim_labour_rebill (state_due; subject service_labour_charge; computes labour_amount)
  declares two overrides. Base service_excl_warranty_or_chargeable's "A customer cannot be billed for labour on a
  line whose charge has been written off as plan covered" is superseded by the rebilling clause (as in revision
  1). Base service_labour_pricing's "raised to the service's minimum hours" is now superseded too (audit
  F-3/O-9): this policy applies the minimum to the dispatch day and to each later attendance of the line that
  carries hours, which reaches a different figure from base's single raise, and that is the tier this world takes.
  Neither superseded clause contains an eligibility condition, so billable_job_state and
  single_billing_basis_per_line stay in force and are evidenced in solvability_contract.
- service_ext_business_contract_relief declares two. Base service_charge_waivers' line cap is superseded because
  this policy caps the relief at the charges standing unsettled on the job (audit O-10). Base
  service_agg_visit_pool's "Included visits are pooled across the profile rather than counted job by job" is
  superseded too: this policy reads the pool from the visits credited and used on the job the relief is granted
  against, which is the same figure wherever a profile holds one work order and a narrower one where it holds
  several. That deviation was found by this revision's own sweep rather than by the audit, and the rule now says
  outright which pool it reads.
- service_ext_invoice_settlement_payment declares none, and the sweep says why: base fixes how a payment is
  applied, this policy fixes how large the settlement is; the rule no longer restates base's application sentence
  or its "in the order they came in" phrasing, neither of which a single scored amount can honour (audit O-17).

FACTOR CARD (tier taken, evidence, baseline figure from the Step 5 run on the amended charter and seed).
service_ext_declined_claim_labour_rebill (6 factors):
 1 rebill_hourly_rate (parameter): the service's own rate / the rate raised by the after-hours percent where no
   surcharge stands booked / the rate recorded. Tier taken: the first — the dispatch day's labour was booked at
   145.00 against the service's 175.00. Baseline (145.00) -> 1035.00.
 2 rebilled_hours_selection (method): the job's hours less the sign-off day's / the job's hours as they stand /
   the dispatch day's hours alone. Tier taken: the first — 9.75 less 2.5 = 7.25. Baseline (6.0) -> 925.00.
 3 minimum_hours_application (method): the minimum applied to the dispatch day and to each later attendance that
   carries hours / the minimum doubled for a single two-person attendance / the minimum applied once to the hours
   taken. Tier taken: the first — two attendance days and a two-person crew, so 6.0 stands and the 1.25 of 9
   September is raised to 2.0, giving 8.0 hours. Baseline (the minimum once, 7.25 hours) -> 1143.75.
 4 rebilled_share_after_decision (parameter, cross-difficulty protection): the whole gross figure to the extent
   of the per-claim limit / nothing / the gross less what the plan has paid out, held to the same limit. Tier
   taken: the first — the plan stands active and the decision of 16 September refused the claim; 1400.00 is well
   inside the 9000.00 limit. Baseline -> 655.00. Revision 3 widened "refused" to every refusal the protection
   charter can record — not covered, outside the term, no proof of purchase, pre-existing — in this factor and in
   the two sibling policies that read the same decision (audit O-26), and guarded the limit read so that on a world
   with no plan active the limit is nothing and the rule says outright that nothing is rebilled there (audit
   O-25): that is what keeps the computation total on the worlds the tier-world test builds.
 5 standing_writeoff_offset (parameter): nothing / the goodwill write-offs / the write-offs standing on the job.
   Tier taken: the first — a 1051.25 plan-cover write-off stands, and the refusal is what reverses it. Baseline
   -> 223.75.
 6 diagnostic_fee_credit (parameter): the figure being rebilled in full / the diagnostic fees standing / nothing.
   Tier taken: the second — 125.00 stands and both diagnoses found a fault. Baseline -> 1400.00.
 Whole baseline -> 0.00 against gold 1275.00 (was 1143.75 in revision 1, before the minimum-hours tiers were put
 the right way round).
service_ext_business_contract_relief (6 factors):
 1 creditable_included_visits (parameter): every visit standing in the pool, where visits granted under a plan
   covering the item stand among them / nothing, where the visits standing were granted only as a gesture of
   goodwill / the visits standing less the planned visits each year. Tier taken: the first — one visit stands and
   it was granted as included in the plan. Baseline (1 less the 2 planned = 0) -> 527.75. Revision 3 re-keyed the
   first tier off the priority queue onto the ground the visit was granted on (audit O-15, the remaining limb), so
   no factor of this difficulty now reads the priority flag; the seeded grant's reason was corrected to the plan
   ground to match (audit O-27).
 2 labour_share_relieved (method): the visits set against the attendances rebilled / the whole of the labour /
   the visits standing against the visits the service includes, counted as at least one (the guard that keeps the
   fall-through total on a service that includes no visits at all — audit O-14). Tier taken: the first — one visit
   against two attendances, so half. Baseline (a quarter) -> 527.75.
 3 crew_attendance_charge_relief (parameter): the charge in full / only the dispatch day's / nothing. Tier taken:
   the first — 89.00 stands and the 2145.00 of labour and parts on 8 September passes the 750.00 waiver figure.
   Baseline -> 757.50.
 4 distance_charge_relief (parameter): the charge standing for the dispatch day / the charges for other days /
   nothing. Tier taken: the first — 45.00 stands for 8 September. Baseline -> 801.50. (Revision 2 re-keyed this
   ladder off the priority queue, which creditable_included_visits already reads, onto the attendance day the
   charge belongs to — audit O-15.)
 5 slot_move_fee_relief (parameter): the fee in full where no write-off on the retailer's own error stands
   against it / what is left of it after such a write-off / nothing. Tier taken: the first — 75.00 stands and no
   write-off stands against it. Baseline -> 771.50. Revision 3 re-keyed the middle tier, which used to read the
   dispatch day, onto the retailer-error write-off, so this policy and the settlement's older-charge ladder treat
   the same fee on the same footing (audit O-31).
 6 plan_met_of_same_work (parameter, cross-difficulty protection): nothing / what the plan has paid out on the
   item / what has been written off to the plan's cover on the job. Tier taken: the first — the claim was
   refused. Baseline -> 0.00. (Revision 2 replaced the per-claim limit in tier 2 with the payouts, matching the
   sibling policy, and replaced the unused coverage pool in the fall-through with the plan-cover write-offs
   standing on the job — audit O-12 and O-13.)
 Whole baseline -> 0.00 against gold 846.50 (was 1352.75).
service_ext_invoice_settlement_payment (6 factors):
 1 invoice_labour_scope (parameter — relabelled from method for consistency with its twin invoice_fee_scope,
   audit O-16): every labour charge / the sign-off day's / the day of settlement's. Tier taken: the first,
   2763.75. Baseline -> 0.00.
 2 invoice_fee_scope (parameter): every fee / the dispatch day's / the sign-off day's. Tier taken: the first,
   334.00. Baseline -> 811.00.
 3 invoice_relief_ground (parameter): every write-off / the plan-covered ones / nothing. Tier taken: the first,
   1897.75. Baseline -> 3042.75.
 4 money_already_held_on_invoice (method): the dispatch day's payment / the payments received / none. Tier taken:
   the second — the only payment is dated 16 September. Baseline -> 1545.00.
 5 next_invoice_deferral (parameter): the day's charges where the job is older than the payment terms / nothing
   where it is inside them / the day's charges together with the fees covered. Tier taken: the second — charges
   were booked today and the work was asked for 25 days back, inside the 30 day terms. Baseline -> 0.00.
   (Revision 2 rebuilt this ladder: the revision-1 tiers shared the conjunct "the profile's invoices run to the
   service's payment terms", which holds of every customer this policy admits, and rested the baseline on a tier
   the scope excluded — audit F-7. The divider is now the age of the job against those terms, which varies across
   the business jobs the policy admits, and the fall-through is reachable by any such job with nothing booked on
   the day of settlement.)
 6 plan_met_on_invoice (parameter, cross-difficulty protection): nothing / the payouts on the item / the
   plan-cover write-offs standing on the job. Tier taken: the first. Baseline -> 93.75. (Same O-13 correction.)
 Whole baseline -> 0.00 against gold 1145.00 (was 507.50).
Every declared baseline is exactly what its policy's baseline.rule states for that input, and each baseline.rule
now states the standard method in plain sentences with no ladder in it and no component left without a method
(audit F-4, F-5, F-6). Multi-source factors: the three plan-decision ladders, creditable_included_visits, the
crew-attendance charge and the slot-move fee, and the deferral ladder. Cross-difficulty: the three protection
ladders.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- service_labour_pricing / billable_job_state: labour billed and payments applied only while the job stands
  dispatched, parts_hold or completed; the job stands completed. Negative case: a job called off could take
  neither write.
- service_excl_warranty_or_chargeable / single_billing_basis_per_line (dedup): one line is either plan work or
  chargeable work, and the flag decides before any charge is booked; the job's warranty flag stands false at
  frozen time, which is what makes the rebill legal, and the line is named in the write. This is the gate the
  first override deliberately leaves standing.
- service_charge_waivers and service_combo_plan_membership_interaction carry no structured gate for
  service_waiver; both enter as policy_scope.
- No time gate is in play.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: work order <SA2>, fleet serial PGD-FLEET-2211, order NB-ORD-5108833, claim
SC-CLM-77412. Lines: PGD-WO-5108833-L1 (the plan-work attendances of 8 and 9 September, their plan-cover
write-off, the trip charge, the diagnostic fee, the slot-move fee, the mileage charge, both diagnoses) and
PGD-WO-5108833-L2 (the sign-off day's labour and the part). The rebill and the relief are booked on L1; the
settlement reads the whole job. Excluded from the rebill: the sign-off day's 2.5 hours on the other line.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS, AND WHAT REVISION 2 CORRECTED IN IT.
- customers <C2>: the business profile; its account type is what makes the contract ground and the payment terms
  apply.
- protection_plans <P2> and five protection ledger rows: the cross-difficulty evidence. Revision 2 corrected
  three seeded values against the protection charter's own arithmetic (audit O-21 and O-22): coverage_remaining
  is now 44380.00, exactly the 45000.00 coverage limit less the one 620.00 payout on file; claims_filed_count is
  2 and repair_attempts_count 1, matching the two claim references and the one repair the ledger carries; and the
  two premium rows are 39.00, the monthly premium the plan's own tier states, not 96.00. No scored figure depends
  on any of the three, and the coverage figure is no longer read by any policy at all after the O-13 fix.
- service_agreements <SA2>: the job, its dates, the priority flag, the two slot moves and the one visit standing.
- the two plan-work labour entries: the hours and the wrongly booked rate; the 1.25 of 9 September is what the
  minimum-hours tier raises.
- the plan-cover write-off: the 1051.25 the refusal reverses.
- the trip charge, the diagnostic fee, the slot-move fee and the mileage charge: the attendance charges the
  contract relieves and the fees the settlement covers.
- the two diagnoses: both find faults, which is what lets the diagnostic fee be credited.
- the sign-off day's labour and the part: always the practice's own.
- the invoice payment of 400.00: the money already held.
- the visit grant and the use: revision 2 changed the grant from four visits on the agreement's renewal to two
  visits credited under the plan covering the item, so one visit stands in the pool after the 8 September
  attendance drew one. That is what makes the contract relief cover half of the rebilled labour rather than all
  of it, which is how the rebill edge came to move the settlement figure (audit F-14).
No cache trap: service_charges_outstanding 716.50 = 2167.75 charged − 400.00 paid − 1051.25 written off, and
visits_remaining 1 agrees with the two ledger rows.

PERSONA. Revision 2 removed the words "put right and" from the opening (audit O-18): he now says he needs the
deployment invoice settled this morning, and that the job is still open on the practice's books, so nothing in
what he volunteers tells the agent that a correction exists. He still confirms the insurers' refusal only if the
agent raises it, still cannot give the hours, the rate or the visits left, and still closes on the transfer being
recorded.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
 root: service_ext_invoice_settlement_payment.
 edge 1: settlement <- contract relief (value_input, gate relief_recognised, form state). Sentence, verbatim from
   the settlement's own rule: "The figure the invoice settles is worked out only after the relief the business
   contract owes stands recorded against the job's charges." Four-point test passed; exactly one write of this
   difficulty books a write-off on a term of the business contract. False at the opening: the job's only
   write-off is on the plan's cover.
 edge 2: contract relief <- rebill (value_input, gate labour_rebilled_today, form state). Sentence, now carrying
   the day as well so that the sentence and the edge's condition have the same scope (audit O-7): "The relief is
   fixed only once the chargeable labour the plan's refusal sends back to the customer stands billed on the job
   on the day the relief is granted." Exactly one write books that entry. False at the opening: the job's labour
   entries are dated 8, 9 and 15 September.
 topological order: rebill, relief, settlement; the customer's own write is the root.
 per-edge deletion sensitivity, recomputed in revision 2 (audit F-12, F-13, F-14): skipping the relief moves
 payment_amount from 1145.00 to 1991.50; skipping the rebill moves relief_amount from 846.50 to 209.00 and
 payment_amount from 1145.00 to 173.50. The second figure is the F-14 fix: in revision 1 the relief covered the
 rebilled labour exactly, so the settlement was 507.50 with or without the rebill and the edge moved only an
 intermediate. With one creditable visit against two rebilled attendances the relief covers half the rebilled
 labour, so the rebill now moves the root problem's own scored figure by 971.50.
 order uniqueness: forced by the two prerequisite sentences. The alternative is recorded honestly — granting the
 relief first gives 209.00 and a settlement of 1782.50, and that order also clears the job to nothing; the
 revision-1 claim that it left the job 1143.75 out was false and has been removed.
 user_scenario mentions neither prerequisite, and no tool validates one.

WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES. Rebilling at the 145.00 the line was booked at; taking only the dispatch day's 6.0
hours; applying the minimum once and billing 7.25 hours instead of 8.0; setting the 1051.25 plan write-off against
the rebill, which the refusal has reversed; forgetting the 125.00 diagnostic credit; treating the 620.00 payout on
the earlier claim as something the plan has met of this work; relieving the whole rebilled labour when only one of
the two attendances is covered by a standing visit; settling the job's whole outstanding figure.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by the registered name, verify on the mobile and the postal code, read the
job, its ledger, the plan and the plan's ledger. Then: (1) rebill the refused line — 7.25 hours taken, the
minimum applied to the dispatch day and to the 1.25 of 9 September giving 8.0 hours, at the service's own 175.00,
1400.00 gross, the whole of it rebilled inside the plan's per-claim limit, the plan-cover write-off not set
against it, the 125.00 diagnostic fee credited: 1275.00 on line PGD-WO-5108833-L1, stamped 8 September; (2) grant
the contract relief — one creditable visit against two rebilled attendances, so half of 1275.00 is 637.50, plus
the 89.00 call-out, the 45.00 distance charge and the 75.00 slot-move fee, nothing off for the plan: 846.50 on the
contract ground; (3) hand the settlement over and have the practice transfer 1145.00 — 2763.75 of labour, 345.00
of parts and 334.00 of fees less the 1897.75 now written off and the 400.00 already received — which clears the
job.

CONSTRUCTIVE TIER-BY-TIER SCORABLE-WORLD TEST. For every tier of every factor of all six policies of the
difficulty — 96 tiers — a world was built that selects that tier and the whole compute was required to return:
96 tiers, 0 failures. On this task's three policies every tier returns, including the no-plan worlds of
rebilled_share_after_decision and plan_met_of_same_work and the fall-through of next_invoice_deferral (tiers 1/2/3
return 0 / 1145.00 / 382.50, so the F-7 fix holds constructively and not only by inspection).

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (revision 3):
  check_compute --task 1 -> 1.json comps 3 fact 18 xfac 3 hist 32 brch 67 step 12 match True, COMPUTE OK
  replay_tasks --task 1 -> 1.json acts 12 det True nonvac True errs 0 clos 22 init 22 match True, REPLAY OK
  check_solvability --task 1 -> 1.json verify True calls 3 base gates 6 seed rows 15 ok True, SOLVABILITY OK
  check_grounding --task 1 -> 1.json idAttrsUsed 2 answers 3 writes 3 cond 12 ok True, GROUNDING OK
  check_extended / check_cross_fire -> EXTENDED OK, SCOPE OK

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP (rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute). Every world-reading or choosing binding quotes
its rule sentence, and every load-bearing rule sentence is claimed by a binding. Revision 2 added the two bases
the audit found unstated (audit O-3): both rules now say how the attendances are counted — "the labour entries
standing on the job other than those booked for the day the job was completed", and for the relief "and those
booked on the day the relief is granted" — matching the expressions exactly. The rule also now states that the
entry the rebill books carries the hours and the rate the gross figure was worked out from while the amount
billed is that gross less the diagnostic credit, so the entry's own fields no longer look like an arithmetic
error (audit O-19).

AUDIT DISPOSITIONS BEARING ON THIS TASK. F-3/O-9: closed by the declared minimum-hours override, and the tier
this world takes is now the declared deviation rather than the coincidence. F-4: closed — the hours ladder is out of baseline.rule, which states the
dispatch day's hours, the minimum applied once and the write-offs standing coming off; the plan-cover sentence
went with it only in revision 3, which is what F-15 caught. F-5: closed — baseline.rule now states the minimum-hours method, and the
factor's baseline is exactly that sentence. F-6: closed for the relief — every component the baseline paragraph
names has its own fall-through sentence. F-7: closed by the rebuilt deferral ladder. F-8/O-11: closed — the rate
uplift applies only where no out-of-hours surcharge stands booked on the job, so the charter never charges the
same hour twice. F-9: closed — the rule now fixes the stamp ("the entry the rebill books is stamped with the day
the crew was dispatched, whatever attendances of that line its hours were drawn from"), so 9 September is excluded
by policy and the gold argument is uniquely entailed. F-12, F-13: the false figures are replaced by the
recomputed 1991.50, 173.50 and the honest both-orders-clear statement. F-14: closed substantively, as described
above. O-3, O-7, O-12, O-13, O-15, O-16, O-17, O-18, O-19, O-21, O-22: closed as described.
F-15: closed — revision 2 left the plan-cover clause inside baseline.rule, which made the declared baseline of
standing_writeoff_offset contradict the paragraph it is supposed to restate. The clause now lives only in the
rule's own ladder ("the write-off the plan's cover carried is not set against the rebilled figure"), baseline.rule
keeps just "From the figure rebilled come the write-offs that already stand on the job", the factor's baseline is
exactly that sentence, and the override declaration is narrowed to the one clause it really displaces.
Revision_2 items bearing on this task: O-25, O-26, O-27, O-29 and O-31 are closed as described in the factor card
and the object card — O-29 by making the rebill's rule say plainly that the entry books one lump for the line
rather than a figure per attendance. O-30: no action, the auditor's own ruling. O-4 and O-6: frozen blueprint
properties, recorded and left. O-8: no action, but the record of revision 2 is corrected — which grounds each
waiver tool accepts is declared in this difficulty's own task_tools.py, so the hop is inside this write domain and
the earlier claim that it was a frozen blueprint property was wrong. It is left as it stands because
check_task_tools requires an enum argument's description to cover the schema's closed set value by value, so
narrowing the accepted grounds would fail the tool-contract gate, and the policy layer already resolves the hop:
only this difficulty's relief rule speaks of a write-off granted on the contract ground.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computes, the expected figures and this
worklog masked: the settlement waits on a contract-ground write-off, and the ledger shows only a plan-covered one;
the relief waits on chargeable labour booked today, and the ledger shows none; so the order is rebill, relief,
settlement. Rebill: the refused line carries labour for 8 and 9 September, so 9.75 less the sign-off day's 2.5 is
7.25; the line has two attendance days and the service sends two people, so the minimum raises the 1.25 to 2.0 and
the hours are 8.0; the dispatch day's labour was booked at 145.00, not the service's 175.00, so the rate is
175.00; 1400.00 gross; the plan refused the claim, so the whole of it is rebilled within the 9000.00 per-claim
limit; the plan-cover write-off is not set against it; the 125.00 diagnostic fee is credited; 1275.00. Relief: one
visit stands in the pool and the job is in the priority queue, so one visit is creditable, and against two
rebilled attendances the share is a half, 637.50, plus 89.00, 45.00 and 75.00, nothing off for the plan; 846.50.
Settlement: 2763.75 + 345.00 + 334.00 − 1897.75 − 400.00, nothing deferred and nothing met by the plan; 1145.00.
Identical to gold.

REVISION 4 — WHAT THE AUDIT'S REVISION_3 ROUND CHANGED HERE. The audit passed this task on all four relationships,
and its one finding, F-19, bears on task 0's membership relief; none of this task's three policies holds a
double-relief mechanism of that shape. Two things moved in the artifacts this task reads. O-33, closed: the text
splice in this policy's minimum-hours ladder is repaired, so the second tier reads as a condition again — "…the
service's minimum hours are applied to the day the crew was dispatched and to the hours of the line's later
attendances taken together, and the two raised figures are added; where the line carries labour for one attendance
day and the service requires two people to attend, the service's minimum hours are doubled and applied to that
attendance." The declaration's replaced_by still matches the rule verbatim, the tier taken is still the first, and
no figure moves: the three golds stand at 1275.00, 846.50 and 1145.00, every factor sensitivity is unchanged, and
the whole-baselines stand at 0.00, 0.00 and 0.00. O-32 is recorded against policy 1, which this task does not
claim. The two standing checks were re-run across the whole difficulty after the change: the constructive
tier-by-tier scorable-world test gives 96 tiers, 0 failures, this task's eighteen-tier policies included, and the
undeclared-deviation sweep over the amended policies found one gap, in task 0's relief, now declared.
user_scenario:
Desmond Yarborough runs the office side of Pinegrove Dental Partners, four surgeries and a small back office,
and he talks the way a practice manager does on a Friday morning: brisk, friendly, one eye on the clock,
because the practice's payment run goes out before noon and he does not want this carried into October. Over
the first two weeks of September a Northbeam crew came in and put the new machines across the surgeries, came
back the next day to finish the network side, and signed the job off in the middle of the month. He rings the
TechWorks business desk because that job is still open on the practice's books and he wants it closed off: as
he says early on, he needs the deployment invoice settled this morning, and the money will go out of the
practice account as a transfer the moment he has a figure to put against it.

He gives the registered name, Pinegrove Dental Partners, straight away, and his mobile, 6125540932, because
that is the number the desk always asks for. If the agent wants another detail to be sure of him he gives the
postal code of the surgery, 55432, and if pressed for the card kept on file he says he thinks it ends 5744 but
would rather the desk did not touch the card. He will read out the order the machines were bought on, NB-ORD
dash five one zero eight eight three three, if that helps, and the serial on the rack label, PGD-FLEET-2211,
if asked. He cannot say what the crew's hours were on either day, nor what rate anyone was charged at, and he
says plainly that the practice only sees the totals; he asks the desk to read those from its own record. He has
no idea how many included visits the contract has left and says as much. If the agent asks how the money is to
be sent he repeats that it will be a bank transfer that morning, and if asked whether the practice would rather
leave it on the account to run to its terms he says no, he wants it cleared today.

He responds rather than pushes. If the agent raises what the insurers said, he says the plan people wrote to
them on Wednesday that they would not be covering it, and that this is exactly why he is ringing. When the
agent explains that the work therefore goes onto the practice's own invoice, he accepts it without argument but
asks for the figure to be read out slowly so the bookkeeper can key it. If he hears there is a charge on the
job for bringing the crew out, he says nobody mentioned a call-out charge when the rollout was booked and asks
the desk to check that against what was agreed. If he is told the contract takes something off the invoice, he
is pleased and says to put whatever the contract allows against it. When the agent hands him something to run
himself so that the transfer is recorded, he does it while they are talking and reads back the reference it
gives him. Once he hears from the agent that the transfer has been recorded and the job is clear, he says that
is the last thing on his list before the payment run, thanks the desk and rings off; he asks for nothing else
and raises nothing new after that.

seed_consistency.check: One work order on this item serial for this work type, standing completed after a sign-off on 15 September: the crew was dispatched on 8 September, the slot had been moved twice against an allowance of three, the job is no longer flagged as plan work after the plan's refusal, and the charges outstanding, 716.50, are exactly the charges booked (2167.75) less the payment received (400.00) and the write-off granted (1051.25). The one visit still included agrees with the two granted and the one used.

Labour for the first attendance of the refused line: 6.0 hours at 145.00 an hour is 870.00. The hours are a whole number of quarter hours and above the service's minimum of two hours, and the rate is not the service's own 175.00 an hour, which is the error the rebilling puts right.
Labour for the second attendance of the same line: 1.25 hours at 145.00 an hour is 181.25, booked the day after the crew was dispatched and on the same line of work.

A write-off of 1051.25 on the ground of the plan's cover, exactly the two plan-work labour entries added together, granted on 9 September while the job was still being treated as plan work and recorded against their line.
The charge for bringing the crew out, 89.00, is the service's trip charge, billed once for the attendance of 8 September.
The diagnostic fee of 125.00 is the service's diagnostic fee, billed once for the attendance at which the fault was found, and the service credits it against the repair where the customer goes ahead.
The fee for moving the slot, 75.00, is the service's reschedule fee, billed once on 31 August at short notice, which agrees with the two moves recorded on the job against an allowance of three.
The charge for the distance travelled, 45.00, is fifteen miles beyond the service's sixty mile radius at its 3.00 a mile, billed once for the attendance of 8 September.

The diagnosis of 8 September records a software configuration fault found on site by the crew assigned to the job, which is a fault found rather than no fault, so the diagnostic fee stands and is credited against the repair.
The diagnosis of 9 September records a network fault found on the same line by the same crew, again a fault found, so no diagnosis on the job reports no fault at all.
Labour for the sign-off day: 2.5 hours at 175.00 an hour is 437.50, at the service's own rate, booked on the second line of work and on the day the job was signed off.
The part billed on the sign-off day is 345.00, a 300.00 part plus the service's fifteen percent markup, booked on the same line as that day's labour.

A payment of 400.00 taken on the business account's invoice on 16 September, the day after sign-off and inside the service's thirty day payment terms, which is why part of the invoice still stands unsettled.

Two included visits credited on 24 August under the ShieldCare plan that covers the fleet item, inside the twelve month visit term the service runs, on the day the work was asked for; the service itself includes four visits in a term, so the pool the plan credited is the smaller of the two and is the pool the contract relief reads.
One included visit used by the attendance of 8 September, carried out by the crew assigned to the job, which leaves one standing in the pool and agrees with the figure on the job.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Find the business profile from the registered name the caller gives, and read back its mobile number, the postal code, the card digits on file and that it is a business profile with a tax exemption certificate.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the practice's deployment job can be read without the profile reference, and the postal code is one of the details used to check who is calling.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller has been verified on the business profile from the two details he states himself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No labour, relief or payment may be moved on the account until the in-session verification stands recorded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the fleet deployment job: the service it runs under, that it stands completed, the day the crew was dispatched and the day it was signed off, the claim reference the work was claimed under, that the work is no longer flagged as plan work, the visits still included, how often the slot was moved, that it stands in the priority queue and the charges outstanding on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The service under which the job runs fixes the hourly rate, the minimum hours, the visit term, the included visits, the trip waiver figure and the payment terms, and the days on the job select which attendances every later figure is worked out from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole working record of the job: the two plan-work labour entries with their hours and the rate they were booked at, the write-off that put them to the plan, the chargeable labour of the sign-off day, the part fitted, the charge for bringing the crew out, the diagnostic fee, the fee for moving the slot, the charge for the distance travelled, the two diagnoses, the invoice payment already received and the included visits granted and used.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every figure in the call is reconciled from these rows — the hours and rate of the refused line, the write-off standing on it, the diagnostic fee to be credited, the attendance charges the contract relieves and the payment already received.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the ShieldCare plan on the fleet item: that it stands active, its coverage window, the coverage still standing on it and its per-claim limit band.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Whether the plan stands active decides which tier of the refusal rule applies, and the coverage standing on it is what the fall-back reading of the invoice would otherwise set against the bill.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what has been booked against the plan: the claim filed for this work, the decision recorded against it, the payout made on an earlier claim on the same item and the premium charged and paid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The decision recorded against the claim is what sends the labour back to the customer, and the payout on the earlier claim is what the fall-back reading would take off instead.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the entry that bills the chargeable labour of an attendance on a job.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock and call pair; it moves nothing on the account by itself.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Bill the labour of the refused line back to the practice as chargeable work, at the service's own rate for the hours of both plan-work attendances, less the diagnostic fee already charged, raising the charges outstanding on the job.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the refused-claim rebilling policy produces this figure, from the hours recorded on the refused line, the service's own hourly rate, the decision recorded against the plan's claim, the write-off standing on the line and the diagnostic fee already billed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_agreement_id: The reference of the fleet deployment job, the only TechWorks job on the profile, returned by the work-order lookup at action 2. Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the TechWorks work order or care agreement the labour was carried out under'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one work order, so no other reference can be passed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The reference of the business profile, returned by the profile lookup at action 0 and used for the verification write at action 1. Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the customer profile being billed, read from that profile before the call'. Uniqueness: one profile matched the registered business name.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.work_order_line_reference: PGD-WO-5108833-L1, the line the plan's claim was refused on, read from the two plan-work labour entries and the plan-covered write-off at action 3. Basis: the rule rebills 'the labour of that line' where a plan's decision refuses a claim, and the tool's contract asks for the line 'the labour is billed on'. Uniqueness: the job carries two lines, and the other one carries the chargeable labour of the sign-off day, which no plan claim was made on.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.visit_date: 2026-09-08, the day the crew was dispatched, read from the job at action 2. Basis: the rule fixes the stamp itself - 'the entry the rebill books is stamped with the day the crew was dispatched, whatever attendances of that line its hours were drawn from' - and the tool's contract asks for 'the day the attendance the labour was carried out on took place'. Uniqueness: the refused line carries attendances on 8 and 9 September and the hours billed are drawn from both, so without that sentence either day would satisfy the tool's contract; the rule settles it on the day the job itself records as the day the crew was dispatched, so 2026-09-09 is excluded by the policy rather than by preference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.labour_hours: 8.0. The line the plan refused carries labour for more than one attendance day, so the hours taken are the hours recorded on the job, 9.75, less the 2.5 recorded for the day it was completed, which leaves 7.25 over two attendances. The line carries labour for more than one attendance day and this service requires two people to attend, so the service's minimum of 2.0 hours is applied to the day the crew was dispatched and to each later attendance of the line that carries hours: the 6.0 of 8 September stands, and the 1.25 of 9 September is raised to 2.0, giving 8.0 chargeable hours. The figure is the chargeable labour the entry records.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.hourly_rate: 175.00. The labour of the day the crew was dispatched was recorded at 145.00 an hour, which is not the service's own hourly rate for TechWorks Business On Site Deployment, so the rate for the rebill is the service's own hourly rate, 175.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.labour_amount: 1275.00. The hours are 8.0 and the rate is 175.00, so the gross figure is 1400.00. The plan covering the item stands active and the decision recorded against its claim refused it as not covered, so the whole of that gross figure is rebilled, to the extent of the plan's per-claim limit of 9000.00, which it is well inside. A write-off granted on the plan's cover stands on the job, so nothing comes off for write-offs already standing. A diagnostic fee of 125.00 stands on the job and both diagnoses recorded on it found a fault, so the diagnostic fee is credited in full. 1400.00 less nothing less 125.00 is 1275.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the entry that relieves a business customer of part of what a job has billed them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock and call pair for the contract relief; it moves nothing on the account by itself.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Relieve the practice of what its contract's included visits should have covered on the rebilled labour, together with the charge for bringing the crew out, the charge for the distance travelled and the fee for moving the slot, lowering the charges outstanding on the job.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the business contract relief policy produces this figure, from the visits standing in the pool, the attendances the rebilled labour covers, the attendance charges on the job and what the plan has met of the same work.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_agreement_id: The reference of the fleet deployment job whose charges are being relieved, returned at action 2. Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the TechWorks work order or care agreement whose charges are being relieved'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one work order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The reference of the business profile, returned at action 0. Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the business profile being relieved of the charges, read from that profile before the call'. Uniqueness: one profile matched the registered business name.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.work_order_line_reference: PGD-WO-5108833-L1, the line the relieved labour and the attendance charges all stand on, read at action 3 and at action 7. Basis: the relief is worked out on the chargeable labour billed on the day the relief is granted, which the rebill booked on this line, and the tool's contract asks for the line 'the relief is granted against'. Uniqueness: the attendance charges of 8 September and the rebilled labour carry this line; the other line carries only the sign-off day's labour and the part.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.relief_amount: 846.50. Two included visits were granted in the visit term under the plan covering the item and one has been used, so one stands in the pool, and because visits granted under a plan stand among them that one visit is creditable. The rebilled labour covers two attendance days and one visit is creditable, so the visits cover one of the two and the share relieved is one divided by two, half of the rebilled labour: half of 1275.00 is 637.50. To it are added the charge for bringing the crew out, 89.00, because the labour and parts booked for 8 September reach the 750.00 at which the service waives it; the charge for the distance travelled, 45.00, because it stands on the job for the day the crew was dispatched; and the fee for moving the slot, 75.00, because no write-off on the retailer's own error stands against it. The plan covering the item stands active and the decision recorded against its claim refused it, so nothing is taken off for what the plan has met. 637.50 plus 89.00 plus 45.00 plus 75.00 is 846.50, which is below the 1991.50 standing unsettled on the job.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.relief_ground: contract_term. Basis: the rule is written for the relief a business profile's contract owes on a job, and the tool's contract gives that value for the case where 'a term of the customer's business contract requires the charge to be relieved'. Uniqueness: the plan's claim was refused, so protection_plan_covered does not hold; the work is not warranty work, so manufacturer_warranty does not hold; the profile holds no Circle membership, so membership_benefit does not hold; nothing on the job arose from a retailer mistake, so retailer_error does not hold; the relief is owed under the contract rather than chosen as a gesture, so goodwill does not hold; and none is only for an entry that records no ground at all.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Hand the practice manager the entry with which he settles the invoice himself, and tell him the reference, the figure and the way the money is to be sent.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Settling the invoice is the business's own act on its own money; he cannot run it until the agent has passed it to him.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The practice settles what the invoice on the deployment job comes to after the rebill and the contract relief, by bank transfer, clearing the outstanding figure on the job.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the invoice settlement policy produces this figure, from the labour, parts and fees the settlement covers, the relief now recognised, the payment already received and what the plan has met of the same work.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_agreement_id: The reference of the deployment job being settled, handed over by the agent from action 2. Basis: the tool's contract asks for the reference of the agreement 'whose invoiced charges are being settled, as the agent hands it over before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one work order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The reference of the practice's own profile, handed over by the agent from action 0. Basis: the tool's contract asks for 'the reference number of the paying business profile, as the agent hands it over before the call'. Uniqueness: one profile matched the registered business name.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_amount: 1145.00. The job stands completed and carries labour for the sign-off day and for earlier days, so every labour charge on it is covered: 870.00 and 181.25 for the plan-work attendances, 437.50 for the sign-off day and the 1275.00 just rebilled, 2763.75 in all. The parts standing billed, 345.00, are covered. Fees stand on the job both for moving the slot and for the distance travelled, so every fee is covered: 89.00, 125.00, 75.00 and 45.00, 334.00 in all. A write-off granted on a term of the business contract now stands on the job, so every write-off standing on it is recognised: 1051.25 and 846.50, 1897.75. Payments stand on the job and none is for the day the crew was dispatched, so the 400.00 already received is taken off. The job carries charges booked today and the work was asked for on 24 August, twenty-five days back and inside the service's thirty day payment terms, so nothing is left for the next invoice; and because the plan's claim was refused nothing has been met by the plan. 2763.75 plus 345.00 plus 334.00 less 1897.75 less 400.00 is 1145.00, which clears the job.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: bank_transfer. Basis: the service's payment methods allowed are 'business invoice or bank transfer' for TechWorks Business On Site Deployment, and the caller says the money will go out of the practice account as a transfer that morning. The tool's contract gives bank_transfer for the case where 'the business sends the money from its bank account'. Uniqueness: business_invoice does not hold because he asks to clear it now rather than leave it on the account; card_on_file and in_store_cash are not methods this service allows; store_credit does not hold because the profile holds no store credit balance.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and the order is forced by the two prerequisite sentences rather than by the terminal state. The relief's own rule says its figure is fixed only once the chargeable labour the plan's refusal sends back stands billed on the job on the day the relief is granted, and the settlement's own rule says its figure is worked out only after the relief the business contract owes stands recorded against the job's charges; each sentence waits on a state that exactly one write of this difficulty brings about, so rebill, relief, settlement is the only order in which each figure is worked out on the world its own rule requires. The recomputation run records what the alternative actually produces, so that nothing rests on a false residue: granting the relief before the rebill gives a relief of 209.00 and a settlement of 1782.50, and that order also clears the job to nothing (3442.75 charged less 400.00 already paid, 1260.25 written off and 1782.50 settled). The two orders are therefore distinguished by the scored amounts (1275.00, 846.50 and 1145.00 against 209.00 and 1782.50), not by whether the job clears.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the contract relief leaves the settlement recognising the plan-covered write-off alone, 1051.25: the scored payment_amount moves from 1145.00 to 1991.50, and the practice pays the whole of the rebilled labour instead of the half the contract relieves.

Skipping the rebill leaves the relief with no chargeable labour to act on: the scored relief_amount moves from 846.50 to 209.00, and the settlement moves too, from 1145.00 to 173.50, because the labour covered falls by 1275.00 while the relief recognised falls by only 637.50 and the day carries no charge, so the fees covered are deferred to the next invoice instead.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller asks only for the deployment invoice to be settled before the practice's payment run, and says nothing about either prerequisite: the words rebill, labour, write-off, relief, contract term, included visit and priority queue never appear in user_scenario, and he drops no hint that anything must be booked first. What he contributes about them is passive: he says the plan people told him the claim came back refused only if the agent raises the claim, he agrees to the labour being put on the practice's own invoice when the agent explains it, and he says he was told nothing about a call-out charge if the agent mentions one. He does not know how many included visits the contract has left and says so if asked, and he no longer says anywhere that the invoice needs putting right.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the three tools checks a prerequisite. bill_uncovered_device_labour_51108cc0 creates its labour entry and updates the job's outstanding figure with no test of any other entry; credit_contract_relief_ce7af535 creates its write-off entry whether or not any chargeable labour stands on the job, and its only conditional reads the job row to keep the running total in step; settle_deployment_invoice_642fded5 books whatever payment amount it is given without comparing it with the charges standing. An agent that settles first still gets a receipt, and the difference appears only in the terminal figures.
